scenes.headline: How Altar-1 cuts a giant model down to four GPUs
scenes.sub: Aikido's security model: GLM-5.3, pruned and quantised to run on-site.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Onyx! Altar-1 is Aikido's security model, built to run inside a customer's own rack. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Take GLM-5.3, delete 88 of the 256 routed experts in every layer, store the rest at four bits, and leave routing untouched.
scenes.say: Take GLM-5.3, delete eighty-eight of its two hundred and fifty-six experts per layer, and store the rest at four bits.

items.say: It starts as GLM-5.3: seven hundred and fifty-three billion parameters at full precision.
A quantised build stores the routed experts at four bits: four hundred and eighty-eight gigabytes.
A prune keeps a hundred and sixty-eight per layer, calibrated on Aikido's pentesting traces and multilingual text.
The result is three hundred and twenty-eight gigabytes. Scales, and the parts never quantised, make that five point two four bits a parameter, not four.

steps.say: In each expert layer, a router sends every token to a few experts.
Pruning shrank the bank it picks from, to a hundred and sixty-eight.
But it still picks eight: about forty billion active parameters, as before. A token costs no less to compute.
What shrinks is memory: it fits on four H200 GPUs instead of six or more.

scenes.title: Which experts you keep matters
scenes.note: KL from the unpruned model at 192 experts; lower is closer
scenes.say: Which experts you keep matters too. At a hundred and ninety-two experts, the best domain plan drifts far less than frequency picking, which is barely better than random.

scenes.label: Altar against its quantised parent, case by case
scenes.note: Every case contains a known CVE, so false positives are never scored
scenes.say: Altar matches its four-bit parent on thirty-one of thirty-two cases. But every case hides a known bug, so false alarms are never scored.

scenes.text: Pruning experts costs prose roughly four times what it costs code, so a code-reading model is the right one to prune.

recap: 88 of 256 experts deleted, the rest at INT4
Routing untouched: memory shrinks, compute per token does not
Matches its parent on 31 of 32 cases
scenes.say: To recap: fewer experts, four-bit weights, the same routing, nearly the same results.
